Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As part of our SIG submission and internal security review, Harbor needs a concise network & boundary narrative that maps to the SIG/CAIQ questions. Specifically we need: 
- A one-page narrative that explains how Redwood separates control plane vs. data plane in Private and Dedicated modes (including optional air-gapped variant).
- L2/L3 diagrams for both Private (customer VPC + private control plane) and Dedicated (Redwood-managed occupant GPU pools + per-tenant fencing).
- A simple segmentation matrix showing traffic types, egress controls, and KMS/HSM touch points.
- A CAIQ mapping doc that points to specific architecture artifacts and evidence (SOC 2 controls, audit logs, VPC flow sampling, KMS keys).

Target: can you get a draft to us by EOD 2027-06-14 so Harbor can include it in their SIG upload? Procurement (Leah) is copied for contractual timeline.

If helpful, we can accept a draft set of diagrams and a short Q&A doc first.

Appreciate it — Daniel

Jasmine / Ben — starting the CAIQ mapping now. High-level notes to include in the narrative (so Ben can slot these into the diagram captions):

- Control plane model: For Private deployments we offer a customer-controlled private control plane (customer VPC peering + private endpoint). Control-plane telemetry is encrypted in transit with TLS1.3 and authenticated via mTLS; control plane does not persist customer data except for routing metadata needed for placement. For Dedicated pools, the control plane sits in a Redwood-managed control VPC with strict IAM and VPC peering; tenant routing is enforced by hypervisor-level process isolation and runtime namespaces.

- Data plane separation: KV caches and model serving processes are namespace-isolated per-tenant. We enforce short-lived ephemeral instance lifecycles and CIDR scoping for tenant pods. Egress is gated by per-tenant NAT instances and egress policies; optional VPC NAT translations and egress proxies are documented in the segmentation matrix.

- Key management: Customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) is supported for Private deployments; Dedicated customers can either bring their key or use Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed key wrapping. Document which CAIQ/CC controls are satisfied and which evidence artifacts we will attach (KMS rotation logs, HSM attestations, key-usage audit).

- Observability & evidence: We will point to SOC 2 log retention windows, per-route tracing tags, audited access logs (control plane admin actions), and sampled VPC Flow logs for egress verification.

- Optional air-gapped variant: brief note on an on-prem/private package: no direct egress, controlled maintenance windows, and local KMS/HSM integration — call out differences in the CAIQ mapping.

Attachments I will produce: harbor_caiaq_mapping_v1.docx (mapping table to CAIQ questions), harbor_segmentation_matrix_v1.xlsx (traffic classes + controls), harbor_sig_response_draft.pdf (narrative + references).

I'll drop first drafts to the Drive by tomorrow morning 2027-06-11 09:00 PT for Ben/Laurn review.

-Kim
